# IZLI Legacy Release Protocol

Version 2.0

Status: Core Platform Protocol

---

# Purpose

This protocol defines the lifecycle of every physical product released by the IZLI Platform.

Every specialized agent must follow this protocol before making product, commerce, community, production, UX or architecture decisions.

This document overrides traditional ecommerce assumptions.

IZLI is not inventory-driven.

IZLI is Legacy-driven.

---

# Core Philosophy

IZLI does not sell permanent products.

IZLI publishes Legacy Releases.

Each Release represents one chapter of the IZLI Legacy.

Every sold-out Release strengthens the Legacy and prepares the next one.

Products are finite.

Legacy is infinite.

---

---

# Business Principles

Every product belongs to:

- one Archive

- one Collection

- one Product

Every Product may have multiple Legacy Releases.

Each Legacy Release is unique.

---

# Legacy Release

A Legacy Release contains:

- Release Number

- Product

- Quantity

- Launch Date

- Status

- QR Experience

- Product Passport

- Production Assets

- Story

- Archive

- Keeper Statistics

- Community Participation

---

# Release Status

Draft

↓

Ready

↓

Production

↓

Upcoming

↓

Live

↓

Sold Out

↓

Archived

No Release may return to Live after Sold Out.

---

# Quantity Rules

Every Release has a predefined quantity.

Examples

150

250

300

500

Unlimited inventory is forbidden.

# Community

Every sold-out Release should activate:

- Voting

- Community Lab

- Challenges

- Rewards

- Referrals

- Archive Discussions

The community participates in shaping the next Release.

---

# Production Rules

Publishing a Release automatically generates:

- Product Identifier

- QR Code

- Product Passport

- Print Assets

- Labels

- Packaging

- Production Package

- Manufacturing Files

Automation is mandatory.

---

# Product Identifier

Format

IZLI-[COL]-[SIZE]-[SERIAL]

Community Lab

IZLI-COM-[SIZE]-[SERIAL]

Identifiers never change.

# Final Principle

Every decision must answer one question:

Does this strengthen the Legacy?

If the answer is no,

do not implement it.
